races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Always Magic
runners_data.note: Ran once, finished 8th over 7f on good — the step down to 5f is sharp and unproven, and despite natural hold-up tendencies, will likely find itself pushed further forward than ideal in a field this deep; fades-in-finish flag is a real concern at the trip.

runners_data.name: Dhikola
runners_data.note: John O'Donoghue in good recent form (T14: 2/3) but both prior runs were 6f+ on good and both yielded double-figure finishes; a hold-up horse naturally, it will be shuffled into a midfield slot it rarely occupies and faces an uphill task getting competitive.

runners_data.name: Eagle Eclipse
runners_data.note: Debut runner for J A Stack, saddled by Seamie Heffernan which is a strong booking — style and going preference entirely unknown, so the key watch is whether it jumps cleanly and settles, as a 5f maiden is unforgiving of a slow start on first appearance.

runners_data.name: Give Me Liberty
runners_data.note: Has three runs at longer trips (6-7f) and finished 6th-7th each time; headgear noted (v) and trainer McCreery has runners in form — however, being a natural hold-up type that cannot settle back on this occasion may blunt the finishing effort it relies on.

runners_data.name: Invincible Irish
runners_data.note: Sole run was a well-beaten 11th over 5f good — exactly this trip and going but showed nothing, and the fades-in-finish flag plus the inability to settle naturally at the back of this large field makes improvement hard to forecast.

runners_data.name: Nando The Great
runners_data.note: Ran just five days ago (fresh concern) and finished 19th over 6f — form is dismal, trainer rate poor (T14: 0/21), and the fades-in-finish flag suggests stamina rather than speed is the issue; hard to see a route to competitiveness.

runners_data.name: Walk On Harry
runners_data.note: De Bromhead yard (T14: 4/34 respectable clip) and the only hold-up type with a placing at this exact trip (3rd over 5f good) — the best-credentialled of the closers and at least has course-relevant fitness; headgear (t) noted, may help concentration.

runners_data.name: Annie Tips
runners_data.note: Single run produced an 8th over 6f — naturally a hold-up type, will be pressed into midfield with no guarantee of a clean run; James Dowling yard is modest in recent form and the step down in trip adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.note: Three starts, all on good ground, all over 5-6f, each a small improvement (6th-5th-4th) — a proper build-up profile and Ben Coen is a top-tier booking; prominent style suits this race shape perfectly and the progression trend is the most visible in the field.

runners_data.name: Best Love
runners_data.note: Has a 4th at exactly this trip on good going and Harty yard is in operation — an unplaced run at 6f good and a 10th on soft are the negatives, but the 5f good form is the relevant line; prominent style is a strong tactical fit here.

runners_data.name: Better Yet
runners_data.note: Debut for Mrs John Harrington with Shane Foley up — both are big-race operators and this pairing rarely appears without a well-prepared horse; style and going preference are unknown but the yard angle makes this the most interesting unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: My Irish Lady
runners_data.note: Murtagh yard with an apprentice (Rory Mulligan, 5lb claim) — two runs both over 5f good, finishing 10th and 6th, the progression is modest; a natural hold-up type in a race that does not favour that style, the claim helps on weight but the tactical situation is tough.

runners_data.name: Ocean Surge
runners_data.note: Ran 8th over 6f good on sole start — fades-in-finish flag and 61 days off (freshness unknown); McCreery has runners in form but this horse was below mid-field on its only outing and the drop to 5f is unproven.

runners_data.name: Southern Boulevard
runners_data.note: The race's pivotal horse — Keane/Lyons combination, sole front-runner, twice placed at exactly 5f good going, and uncontested lead on a flat track is a significant tactical advantage; the race map is built around what it does.

runners_data.name: Stormy Dawn
runners_data.note: Sole run was 12th over 7f good — this 5f drop is dramatic and unproven, fades-in-finish flag suggests stamina limits rather than a speed profile; P A Fahy yard modest in form and the apprentice booking (Kennedy, 5lb) does not add confidence.

runners_data.name: Syrah
runners_data.note: Charles Weld debut runner with an apprentice jockey (McGettigan, 5lb) — Weld occasionally sends lightly-raced types in good shape but the booking is not a headline signal; going and style completely unknown and the 5lb claim is the only concrete angle to note.

races.paceDynamic: Southern Boulevard is the lone confirmed front-runner and, ridden by Colin Keane for G M Lyons, will stride straight to the front from the gates and control a steady, uncontested gallop over this flat 5f on good turf. With no genuine rival pressing for the lead, the pace is likely to be moderate early before Keane decides when to lengthen, creating a race that rewards those who can travel close to the speed and produce a clean, sharp finish rather than a deep late run. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can all settle into their natural position — Invincible Irish, Give Me Liberty, Dhikola, Annie Tips and Always Magic are true hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded, meaning several will be forced further forward than suits and their finishing kicks will be compromised. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can slot in just behind Southern Boulevard and pounce off a slow-moderate pace, while genuine closers face a traffic and positioning problem that makes their task markedly harder.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Southern Boulevard Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Southern Boulevard leads from the off and sets a comfortable, gallop-your-own tempo with no rival able to lock on.
scenarios.body: Colin Keane dictates every yard on the flat 5f, dictating a pace that suits his own mount before kicking clear in the final furlong; horses that travel prominently just off the leader get the cleanest run and best shot at pegging him back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chasers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent horse settles just behind Southern Boulevard and sustains the better finish over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The moderate pace set by Southern Boulevard allows one or two prominent racers to travel in a perfect stalking position and quicken past in the closing stages; Arrowstock and Best Love, who have course-relevant 5f form on good ground, are ideally positioned to exploit this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Upsets On Raw Ability
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed newcomers — Eagle Eclipse, Better Yet or Syrah — possesses superior raw ability and overcomes positional uncertainty.
scenarios.body: A debut winner on a flat track in good ground can paper over any tactical naivety, particularly if the trainer has the horse forward-fit; Shane Foley aboard Better Yet (Harrington yard) and Seamie Heffernan on Eagle Eclipse represent the strongest formbook connections among the unknown trio.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded hold-up group splits into gaps late and a true closer threads through to grab a placing.
scenarios.body: This requires an unusually clean split through sixteen runners on a flat 5f, making it a low-probability outcome given the style congestion; Walk On Harry, who has at least placed at this trip and trip on good, is the most credible beneficiary if it does materialise.

watchPoints.text: Southern Boulevard (Keane/Lyons) is the only confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse field — if it breaks cleanly and immediately establishes the lead, it may control the entire race from an uncontested position with no rival capable of hunting it down early.

The hold-up group (Invincible Irish, Always Magic, Annie Tips, Dhikola, Give Me Liberty) are all effectively racing out of their preferred position today — watch for early crowding and interference in the first two furlongs as these horses are forced to compete for space they would not normally occupy.

Arrowstock has shown steady improvement across three consecutive runs at exactly this trip and surface, and with Ben Coen aboard in a prominent position, it represents the clearest progressive profile in the race — a step forward here would not be a surprise.

Better Yet (Harrington/Foley) and Eagle Eclipse (Stack/Heffernan) are the two best-connected debutants — watch how quickly they jump and whether they travel to the pace in the opening furlong, as that will immediately indicate whether they have been prepared for a winning run.

Walk On Harry is the one hold-up horse with an actual placing at 5f good going — if gaps appear in the straight, it is the most likely of the rear-of-field types to arrive with a meaningful late challenge, and the De Bromhead T14 strike rate of 4/34 is worth noting.

races.name: OCS Recruitment Handicap

runners_data.name: Kiss Don't Tell
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Daniel McLoughlin — returned to 5f here is a positive given her only placing came over 5f, but 254 days off the track is a significant freshness flag and her form string tails off; Ben Coen's booking for a yard without a recent winner is an angle worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Amerilis
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with two Good-ground placings at 5f from seven tries in similar conditions — Donagh O'Connor takes the ride for Gillian Scott, she drops back from 6f trips where she has been consistent, and the tongue strap is confirmed headgear; 34-day freshness is straightforward.

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 27 days off for A Oliver, whose yard has been in form (3/11 in 14 days) — her one placing at 5f came on Soft so a step up in surface speed is required on Good, and the tongue tie is noted; Sam Coen claims 5lb which helps offset the OR.

runners_data.name: The Right One
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who clearly relishes 5f on Good ground (eight of ten runs on similar surface, four places) and won on Soft last time out — Ronan Whelan rides for Fahey, and the 34-day gap is normal; the question is whether Cashel Blue presses hard enough to undermine her chance.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won at 5f on Good at Cork and has the strongest recent form profile of the pace-setters — W J Lee is a significant booking for K J Condon, and the trainer landed a winner in the past 14 days; Cashel Blue is likely to be the pace horse that remains most competitive late if the duel is managed.

runners_data.name: Lilbittyprettyone
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for David Marnane with Rebecca Parsons claiming 10lb — only one run on Good going from four recorded and all recent form is off Soft, making the surface a genuine query; 33-day return is routine but her career best RPR came at 5f on Soft, not Good.

runners_data.name: Smart Sioux
runners_data.note: Flagged as prone to fading in the finish, has not run for 125 days and all recent finishes are deep in the field — the tongue tie is noted but her Good-ground record shows only mid-division at best, and the layoff combined with finishing concerns makes this a watch-and-see profile.

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator by style but the depth of the hold-up population here means she is likely to end up in midfield rather than at the rear — Seamie Heffernan is a quality booking for Rodger Sweeney, and her only Cork form came on Good (13th at 5f), suggesting track familiarity is limited; finishing fade flag applies.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose natural position will be compromised in this pace-heavy field — 125 days off for Daniel James Murphy is a notable freshness concern, all five recent runs have placed her in the bottom half of the field, and the fade-in-finish flag is a further deterrent; Terry Casey claims 7lb.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good (eight of ten runs in similar conditions) and has shown she can find a prominent position when needed — Orla Tynan claims 7lb for Miss Jennifer Anne Lynch, and the 11-day turnaround is the freshest in the field; her true hold-up tendency may be masked by the headgear (p) note.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Flat in a different going type but her Cork 5f Good record shows a placing — Nathan Crosse is an amateur booking, she has been off 77 days, and her natural hold-up style is compromised by the field's back-heavy composition; best viewed as a each-way outsider in a collapse scenario.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for W McCreery whose trainer is in form (3/14 last 14 days) — visor is noted headgear and she has finished fourth and eighth in Good-ground 5f and 6f, but the fade flag and the redistribution from rear mean her true style is unlikely to be expressed; Megan Telford-Kelly claims 7lb.

races.paceDynamic: The Right One and Cashel Blue are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 5f on Good ground at Cork, guaranteeing a genuinely contested pace rather than a dawdle. With two horses committed to setting the fractions, the early sectionals should be honest to brisk, making this a true test of speed and stamina for a 5f handicap. This race shape structurally favours prominent racers who can travel close to the contested pace without burning energy fighting for position — runners like Kiss Don't Tell and Amerilis, who can slot in behind the battle and pounce, are best placed. The field contains a cluster of true hold-up horses — Sceitimini, Simmering Seas, Another Nice'day, Love Bomb, and Lady Landhort — who are unlikely to secure their natural position at the rear given the compressed field dynamics and are mapped to midfield, meaning genuine late-closing shapes are discounted; the pace scenario that rewards runners racing prominently or in close pursuit is the one that dominates this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If The Right One and Cashel Blue force a true pace and both begin to tire in the final furlong, leaving a prominent tracker to inherit the advantage.
scenarios.body: The two pace-setters burn each other off over the first three furlongs, and a horse who has settled just behind the duel — travelling without fighting — explodes into the gap. Kiss Don't Tell's prominent style and prior placed effort at 5f on Good suits this shape precisely, and Amerilis's closing habits over 5f on Good (two placings in similar conditions) align with the final-furlong rewards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Cashel Blue — is able to establish a fractional lead and the rival front runner cannot sustain the duel past halfway.
scenarios.body: Cashel Blue has won at 5f on Good at Cork and carries fitness from a 34-day absence, with W J Lee aboard to control tempo; if The Right One fades or stumbles in the contested exchange, Cashel Blue's tactical speed and race-fitness allow her to steal enough of a buffer to hold on. The Right One, with four places from 5f on Good ground and Ronan Whelan's experience, remains the most dangerous to deny if roles reverse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the contested duel between The Right One and Cashel Blue is significantly more fierce than anticipated, causing both to stop sharply and gifting ground to midfield runners.
scenarios.body: Runners mapped to midfield — including those redistributed from the hold-up group like Sceitimini and Another Nice'day — would benefit most, but their true hold-up style means they are unlikely to be positioned close enough to capitalise fully, reducing the reliability of this shape. Amerilis, with a genuine habit of finishing through from rear positions and solid form in Good-ground sprints, is the most credible beneficiary if this scenario does develop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rough Race, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace creates traffic and bunching in the midfield pack, enabling a lightly-exposed or freshened-up runner to thread through at long odds.
scenarios.body: Gonna Be Golden showed a placed effort at 5f on Soft and steps back to a trip where she has shown form, while Lady Landhort won at OR 48 and carries freshness from 77 days off. Both sit at the outer reaches of the field and are unlikely winners, but chaotic pace scenarios occasionally produce big-priced results in 12-runner handicaps on a flat 5f course.

watchPoints.text: The Right One and Cashel Blue — watch the first furlong closely; if both commit fully to the lead the pace will be genuinely hot and both could be spent before the final furlong, dramatically altering which runners can close.

Kiss Don't Tell — 254 days off the track is the longest absence in the field; watch the market move and her behaviour in the preliminaries as signs of readiness before drawing conclusions about her chance as a prominent type.

Sceitimini, Simmering Seas, Another Nice'day, Love Bomb, and Lady Landhort — all genuine hold-up horses forced toward midfield by the race shape; watch whether any manages to slot closer than expected at the start, as that would change their finish position probability materially.

Cashel Blue's early positioning — W J Lee may attempt to dictate rather than be dictated to; if Cashel Blue settles into a rhythm ahead of The Right One rather than fighting stride for stride, the lead scenario shifts heavily in her favour and the race shape becomes less truly contested.

Gonna Be Golden — A Oliver's yard is in a 14-day purple patch (3/11) and Sam Coen's 5lb claim brings her into a competitive weight bracket; worth tracking in the market as a potential trainer-form angle in a wide-open bottom half of this handicap.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Firville Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Alpine Wedding
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with placed form in similar going (3rd on good over this exact trip); trainer Twomey has 2 from 8 in the 14-day window and the step back to 7f after a soft-ground run is the key angle — watch how she handles the increased pace competition.|

runners_data.name: Alwaysanangel
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good at the Curragh last time and now faces a step up to 7f for Joseph O'Brien; a natural hold-up runner who will be ridden to produce late, Dylan Browne McMonagle ideally suited to covering ground from off the pace — the extra furlong should suit on pedigree.|

runners_data.name: Beibhinn
runners_data.note: Four career starts show a progressive filly with a win over 6f on good for O'Brien; her instinct is to race close to the pace, but in a field this well stocked with front-runners, she may not get her preferred position — headgear (pads) noted, and the drop back from recent soft-ground form to good is a positive.|

runners_data.name: Celtic Moon
runners_data.note: Winner over 8f on good at the Curragh for Murtagh last time, then disappointing when tried on soft; reverts to good ground here which is a clear plus, but like several others she prefers to race prominently and finding that berth in this traffic-heavy early fraction will be the challenge.|

runners_data.name: Damsel In Distress
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good on debut before a disappointing 5th at 6f — the return to further (7f) and back to good ground suits, and Ben Coen has strong recent form; McLoughlin's yard is quiet with 0 from 7 in 14 days but the horse's own profile reads well for this.|

runners_data.name: Film Set
runners_data.note: Has run once, finishing 5th over 6f on good for Aidan O'Brien — Ronan Whelan takes over and the step to 7f is the obvious logical move; as a hold-up type with limited form, she is an unknown quantity but the stable's 9 from 34 strike rate in 14 days keeps her in the conversation.|

runners_data.name: Madam Secretary
runners_data.note: The co-pace-setter with Ryan Moore — three career starts all placed, all on good ground, all over 6-7f at Cork and the Curragh; her form figures of 3-3-2 show consistent improvement and Moore's presence at the head of affairs makes her the race-shaper to watch.|

runners_data.name: Maeda Matsu
runners_data.note: Second on debut over 6f on good for Lavery — a lightly raced prominent runner stepping up to 7f; the trainer is quiet (0 from 9 in 14 days) and she faces a significant step up in class at Listed level, but the good-ground form and extra furlong could bring improvement.|

runners_data.name: Maire Rua
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good on debut for Lyons — exactly this trip and going combination, and Colin Keane retains the ride; one run is limited evidence but that debut win profile, travelling prominently and finding plenty, is an ideal blueprint for this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Nevermindtherain
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner for Aidan O'Brien — form figures of 5-5-3-3 suggest a horse who competes consistently without winning; will be asked to make the pace and could be vulnerable late, but pressure from Madam Secretary may stop either controlling the fractions cleanly.|

runners_data.name: Shi Yang
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good at Gowran last time for De Aguiar, having been well beaten over 5f — the step up in trip clearly suited and he arrives in form; his natural front-running tendencies are unlikely to find full expression given the queue for those positions, which is the critical context for assessing his price.|

races.paceDynamic: Nevermindtherain and Madam Secretary are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off over Cork's 7f on good ground, creating a genuine, honest gallop rather than a falsely-run sprint. With Ryan Moore aboard Madam Secretary and Wayne Lordan on Nevermindtherain, neither rider will surrender the initiative cheaply, so the pace should be sustained throughout the trip. This race holds more prominent-natured types than the map can accommodate — Beibhinn, Shi Yang, and Celtic Moon are all natural front-of-field runners, but with two already committed to the lead, Beibhinn (O'Brien, highest OR of the three) is best placed to secure a front-rank berth, while Shi Yang and Celtic Moon are most likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal. A genuinely contested, honest pace over 7f on good turf most directly benefits prominent horses that can travel just off the leaders and pick up through the final quarter, or hold-up horses with the class and acceleration to pounce from mid-division — this race shape tilts toward the prominent-to-midfield profile with genuine quality.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Nevermindtherain and Madam Secretary set a true gallop and the race is run at an even tempo throughout
scenarios.body: The two front-runners pull the field along at a genuine clip, leaving those who travel prominently just off them ideally poised to strike in the final furlong; horses with the class to hold a position and quicken get first run on the hold-up types. Alpine Wedding, Damsel In Distress, and Maire Rua — all capable of racing prominently — are the profiles that benefit from this shape, as they can track the pace without burning petrol and pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners press hard enough early that they fade late, leaving a vacuum for hold-up horses to fill
scenarios.body: Alwaysanangel and Film Set, both natural hold-up runners with strong trainer representation from Aidan and Joseph O'Brien, are able to produce a sustained late run as the pace crumbles in the final furlong. Alwaysanangel brings two runs of good-ground form at 6f and now steps up to 7f for the first time with Dylan Browne McMonagle, who will be confident covering ground from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders, most likely Madam Secretary under Ryan Moore, gets away cleanly and controls a steadier early fractions
scenarios.body: Moore settles Madam Secretary into a comfortable rhythm at the front, the pace is less brutal than expected, and she proves strong enough to last home having conserved energy early; her consistent placed form over this course and trip on good ground underlines her suitability to the scenario. The field chases but, with the honest early trade not materialising, hold-up horses are caught flat-footed and prominent types cannot get past.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Field Aids Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the contested lead causes a bunching effect and multiple prominent horses are shuffled back, creating an unusual race shape
scenarios.body: Shi Yang, despite being forced out of role in this competitive field, showed a sharp turn of foot to win over 7f on good at Gowran and could find a clear run if the race fragments mid-race; Celtic Moon, a winner over 8f on good, handles the trip but needed the gallop to soften the ground ahead of them. This scenario depends on the redistribution resolving in favour of one of the lower-rated horses getting a dream run, which is the least likely outcome against classier rivals.

watchPoints.text: Madam Secretary and Nevermindtherain are both confirmed front-runners and Ryan Moore versus Wayne Lordan over the first furlong could produce a fast, potentially damaging early pace — watch how hard each is asked to lead in the first two furlongs, as that will determine whether the race is truly run or collapses late.

Beibhinn, Shi Yang, and Celtic Moon are all natural prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred early position — watch the start and first quarter-mile to see which, if any, gets slotted in and which is forced to settle further back than ideal, as this will materially affect their chances.

Maire Rua is unbeaten in one start over exactly this trip and going — Colin Keane will be intent on tracking the pace and any crowding or slow break for a lightly raced filly could leave her with too much to do at Listed level.

Alwaysanangel steps up to 7f for the first time having won over 6f — Dylan Browne McMonagle will be patient and cover ground late; the hold-up profile only pays off if the pace is genuinely honest, so monitor early splits relative to previous 7f times at Cork today.

Film Set is a single-run maiden stepping into Listed company for Aidan O'Brien — stable's 9/34 in-form rate is strong but this is a significant ask; watch how she settles in the early stages as she is a completely unknown quantity over this trip in a tactical race.

races.name: NFP Irish EBF Platinum Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Fort Vega
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with an excellent record on good going (10 from 15 similar runs), likely to be positioned last or second-last by Rory Cleary and will need a clear outside passage late; 23 days since last run is a standard return for Sheila Lavery.

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: A 6yo with multiple wins on good ground, races genuinely from the back for Lynam and Lee; the 7f trip is longer than her usual 5-6f range which is a stamina question worth noting, but she has the finishing speed to exploit gaps if they appear.

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Stepped back from 8-10f trips to 7f; the prominent style means she wants to be close to Spinning Around but her form at this distance is thin (one placing in 15 similar-going runs at shorter) and the step up in class to Listed is demanding.

runners_data.name: Nancy J
runners_data.note: Heffernan partners a filly who is naturally a hold-up type but with the rear of the field crowded with closers she is likely to find herself in a midfield berth rather than her preferred position — that compromise means she may neither lead nor get the deep-late run she needs.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: McMonagle takes over on a mare who often races from hold-up and whose good-ground form is solid; 82 days off is the longest layoff in the field and fitness has to be an honest query despite the Ballydoyle handler's strong overall numbers.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by record but pushed forward to midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; her recent form shows a sequence of 5-8-6-11 finishes and her OR of 84 is the lowest in the field, making it hard to see her winning even if she finds her preferred position.

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: Narrow build of form over 7-8f with two recent wins and two seconds, and she carries a hood that likely keeps her focused in a congested prominent group; Shane Foley is adept at finding cover and she has the tactical speed to sit just off Spinning Around.

runners_data.name: L L Koulsty
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3yo who has won his last two over 7f on good ground; the small sample on similar going (2 from 7) is a flag, but the upward trajectory and Rory Mulligan's local knowledge give him an angle, and he has the natural pace to sit in the prominent cluster.

runners_data.name: Sindagan
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners a 3yo with a 1-2-3 placed record in his last four, all at 7f, with good ground wins; he sits right in the sweet spot for this race shape — prominent, distance-proven, and currently in form.

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field; Gavin Ryan should land a soft lead from an inside draw and the task for rivals is to get close enough early without burning extra gas chasing — her two wins have both come over 7f and her good-ground form is acceptable.

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners a 3yo with an unblemished good-ground record (7 from 7 on similar going) and a 7f course win; a prominent style that suits this race shape exactly and Keane's ability to find the right position off a single leader makes her an ideal profile for Scenario A.

runners_data.name: Tahcawin
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll's 3yo has been stepping up in trip from 6f and showed promise with a placing at 6f good ground recently; a genuine hold-up type who will need the race to develop in his favour and whose nine most recent effort on good ground suggests he is still learning.

races.paceDynamic: Spinning Around is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Gavin Ryan should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over Cork's 7f on good ground — fast enough to be legitimate but not so fierce as to collapse the field. Behind her, five runners — Carolina Jetstream, Treasure Rose, L L Koulsty, Sindagan and Suzie Songs — all want prominent positions, creating a congested second rank where traffic incidents between the 2f and 3f poles are a real risk as the race begins to develop. The hold-up brigade is deep: Fort Vega, Keke, Princess Child and Tahcawin all want to come late, and with the pace expected to be sustainable rather than searingly strong, there is a danger that the front end simply does not come back far enough to reward pure closers. This shape — a controlled lead, a bunched midfield, and a clean run to the line — most favours a prominent, prominent-to-handy runner who can travel comfortably just off Spinning Around and pounce from a position of coverage. The field carries more hold-up horses than can all get their natural position; Nancy J and Temperance, both genuine hold-up types by record, are mapped to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed, and neither should be assumed to enjoy the conditions that shape usually demands of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Around dictates a fair but uncontested gallop and the prominent pack tracks smoothly behind her.
scenarios.body: Spinning Around sets a regulated tempo, keeping the field together into the straight where the prominent-placed runners have the position and momentum to strike decisively; a soft pace-collapse in the final furlong is unlikely but the best-placed horse just off the leader benefits most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion forces an untidy race and Spinning Around's leader is never seriously pressed until too late.
scenarios.body: With rivals burning energy sorting out positions 3f out, Spinning Around gets a soft lead and Ryan nurses her into the straight with a decisive advantage; a truly uncontested front-runner on good ground over 7f can be very hard to reel in when the chasing pack was disorganised.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Benefit From Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent five-horse scrum produces significant interference 2-3f out, opening a rail or outer gap for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Fort Vega and Keke, both well-credentialled on good going, could sprint through a gap if a scramble mid-race creates the gaps hold-up horses require; this scenario demands near-ideal traffic management which is far from guaranteed with five prominent runners jostling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Slips Through Unnoticed
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and an overlooked mid-division horse produces a career-best.
scenarios.body: A hot pace would be out of character given Spinning Around faces no direct challenge, but if the prominent battle does quicken things, a lightly-raced improver like L L Koulsty could find a seam late; this remains the least likely shape given the expected tempo.

watchPoints.text: The five-horse prominent cluster — Carolina Jetstream, Treasure Rose, L L Koulsty, Sindagan and Suzie Songs — all want to track Spinning Around closely; watch the first 2f for jostling as they sort hierarchy, with those drawn widest at highest risk of losing ground early.

Nancy J and Temperance are natural hold-up types placed in midfield on the map due to overcrowding — if either tries to drop in naturally they will be further back than ideal, and if they push up to midfield they race out of role; monitor whether Heffernan and Hayes settle for compromise positions.

Spinning Around's lead is unconditional only if no prominent runner breaks sharply and tries to contest it — if Suzie Songs or Sindagan bowls along at her girth, the tempo could lift materially and Scenario B collapses entirely.

Princess Child is the freshest horse in the field at 82 days off; Dylan Browne McMonagle may ride her conservatively early and only ask late — if the pace is genuine she could be finishing strongly but Joseph O'Brien's trainer strike rate in the last 14 days (9/65) suggests normal throughput rather than a targeted return.

Keke's trip is 1-2f longer than her preferred distance; if the pace is steady and the field bunches, her sprint finish may fire, but if the race is truly run at a 7f tempo she will be asked questions of stamina that her recent form at 5-6f cannot fully answer.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Give Thanks Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Ankara
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Joseph O'Brien who faded badly last time at 10/14f in heavy-ground conditions; the return to Good and a firmer surface is a positive, but her record in similar going is 0 wins from 1 placing and she has a worrying tendency to empty in the stretch.

runners_data.name: Bosphorus Rose
runners_data.note: Comfortable prominent racer who won over 12f on Good at the Curragh and boasts a productive similar-going record (3W5P from 13 runs); the step back to Group 3 level suits and she arrives on a sound 45-day freshener for Pat Twomey.

runners_data.name: Nyra
runners_data.note: Well-related O'Brien filly handled by Dylan Browne McMonagle, showing consistent prominent form with five places from seven runs on similar ground including two second-place efforts over today's trip and shorter; the 27-day gap looks ideal.

runners_data.name: Snapretend
runners_data.note: A genuine front-running or close-prominent type by instinct who will struggle to access that position in this traffic-heavy field; style-fit is compromised (0.94 discount flag), so discount accordingly, though the 83-day absence makes her pace and condition harder to read.

runners_data.name: Amelia Earhart
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this Aidan O'Brien three-year-old who has won twice at trips up to 12f on Good but has run only once in the past 13 days and has finished fifth or worse in her last three outings including at today's 14f trip; prominent headgear flag and recent form are both concerns.

runners_data.name: Believed
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's mount is a naturally prominent racer who has been mapped to midfield because the race shape leaves no room — her true instinct is to race close up, and if she cannot find that berth her chance is structurally weakened; has placed three times in five Good-ground starts for Murtagh though.

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Second-string Aidan O'Brien entry who broke a maiden nicely over 12f on Good but has since run three consecutive anonymous efforts including an eighth at 12f Good last time; prominent style but fading away from the yard's better options.

runners_data.name: Caught U Sleeping
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, stepping up in distance after a progressive sequence of 1W2nd over 10f on Good ground; Colin Keane knows exactly how to exploit an uncontested lead and the 41-day freshen should leave her sharp enough to see out the 14f.

runners_data.name: Ice Dancer
runners_data.note: Tail-end Aidan O'Brien runner with five consecutive finishes of seventh or worse; the blinkers flag suggests a behavioural concern and the yard's limited 14-day strike rate on this evidence means she enters as the outsider of the team with very little to recommend her on current form.

races.paceDynamic: Caught U Sleeping is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane in the saddle, should slot comfortably onto an uncontested lead through the 1m4f trip on Good ground at Cork. Behind her, Bosphorus Rose, Nyra, Amelia Earhart, and Cameo all want prominent positions, creating a congested second tier that will compress the early order and could force scrimmaging between the 2f and 3f poles. Snapretend and Believed are genuine prominent types who are unlikely to secure their natural berth given how many runners are pressing for that ground — both are mapped to midfield but will not be true hold-up horses by instinct, meaning the race shape is built around Caught U Sleeping dictating an honest but manageable tempo. This scenario — a single pace-setter controlling fractions while a crowded prominent group jostles behind — classically favours resolute, well-rated closers and milers stepping up in trip who can travel through the early traffic before unleashing a sustained finish, giving the edge to genuine hold-up horses and those able to travel sweetly off a sound but unexaggerated gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caught U Sleeping Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Caught U Sleeping leads unchallenged and sets a fair, metronomic pace that keeps the prominent group honest without burning them off.
scenarios.body: Keane dictates from the front, the prominent bunch never truly pegs him back, and the race only quickens in the final 2f — a genuine test of quality rather than stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent tier (Nyra, Bosphorus Rose, Amelia Earhart) applies collective pressure to Caught U Sleeping early, lifting the tempo and turning the race into a more searching examination.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field on the run to the home turn, breaking up the traffic bottleneck and bringing the closers into play later than usual.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle burns sufficient petrol in the middle mile that true hold-up runners can peel wide and finish powerfully through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Ankara and Ice Dancer, given clear daylight on the outside from 2f out, can sustain their runs to the line — though both carry form concerns that make this a secondary chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Disrupts
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types clash aggressively from the start, causing pace irregularities and positional shuffling that scrambles the expected order entirely.
scenarios.body: The unsettled framing benefits whichever runner can find a clean route through trouble and is travelling best at the 2f pole — Believed and Snapretend, pressed out of position, would have most to gain from pure chaos.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion behind Caught U Sleeping — Bosphorus Rose, Nyra, and Amelia Earhart all want the same second-tier berth and early barging between the 2f and 3f marks is a real risk that could unsettle multiple runners.

Snapretend and Believed are both genuinely prominent types forced into midfield by the race shape; watch for them pushing forward from the break and disrupting the order rather than settling as their mapped position suggests.

Caught U Sleeping's stamina over 1m4f is unproven at this level — if her fractions drift wide in the back straight, the prominent group will sense weakness and accelerate earlier than expected, collapsing the lead scenario.

Ankara fades in the finish (flagged) and holds only 1 place from 4 similar-going runs; monitor her position at the 2f pole — if she is not moving well at that point she is unlikely to produce a late run.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Chosen One
runners_data.note: Donnacha Aidan O'Brien's lightly tried 3yo showed some promise when third over 8f on Good ground but a true hold-up operator who will be squeezed for space at the rear with so many closers in the field, effectively forcing her to race closer to the pace than she would prefer.|

runners_data.name: Elusive In Mayo
runners_data.note: High OR of 120 yet only one run on record — a distant 12th on Soft over 12f — and the fades-in-finish warning combines with the redistribution reality that her natural come-from-behind style may be compromised by the sheer volume of hold-up horses competing for the same ground.|

runners_data.name: Emily Estherfaye
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U) with a single run showing an 11th on Soft over 12f and a fades-in-finish flag; Andrew Slattery's yard has been in decent form (3/31 T14) but there is too little known about her tactical preferences to place confidence in any specific scenario.|

runners_data.name: Fairylike
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed debutante for the formidable A P O'Brien/Wayne Lordan combination, with going and distance unknown; the powerful trainer strike rate (9/34 T14) means she cannot be dismissed but she is essentially a wildcard in pace terms.|

runners_data.name: Garden Party
runners_data.note: The race's key pace figure — Ryan Moore's mount for A P O'Brien bounced back from a 291-day absence and has placed twice in seven-furlong Good-ground races, stepping up markedly in trip; if fit enough, her ability to dictate a solo, unhurried gallop gives her a significant structural advantage.|

runners_data.name: Quinchy Lady
runners_data.note: Two 11th-place finishes on Good over 8f in her entire form record and a consistent fades-in-finish flag leave little reason for encouragement; Siobhan Rutledge rides, but the hold-up style is the wrong tool for a likely slowly-run solo-leader race.|

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for Joseph Patrick O'Brien, who has been busy (9/65 T14), but Salamina's sole run was an 11th on Good over 10f and the fades-in-finish concern makes her a risky proposition in a race that may not produce the late pace required.|

runners_data.name: Saxony Charms
runners_data.note: The field's most natural tracking horse — Colin Keane's mount has placed twice on Good over 10f and arrives 49 days fresh; a prominent style that slots directly behind Garden Party in the early stages makes Saxony Charms structurally well placed if the leader weakens.|

runners_data.name: Serendipia
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners a horse with some consistency in form (3-4 finishes on Good over 8f) and a placed run over 10f, but her natural hold-up style is genuinely constrained here — forced to race from midfield rather than off the back of the field by the volume of closers in the race.|

runners_data.name: The Blonde Lady
runners_data.note: A J Martin runner with no form on record and an unknown going preference; Robbie Colgan rides but there is simply no evidence base from which to draw meaningful pace or tactical conclusions.|

runners_data.name: Trumph
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides for Mrs John Harrington, but Trumph's record — 16th on Soft, 8th on Good — allied to a fades-in-finish flag suggests she needs more pace than Garden Party is likely to generate, making the scenario she requires an unlikely one.|

runners_data.name: Zadawa
runners_data.note: D K Weld's consistent mare has placed twice over 10f on Good ground and Chris Hayes keeps the ride; shown headgear (h) and a hold-up style, she is among the more experienced and proven hold-up types here, though the race shape favours those who travel closer to the pace.|

races.paceDynamic: Garden Party is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Ryan Moore in the saddle for the powerhouse O'Brien yard, she is near-certain to control proceedings from the front at a measured, sustainable tempo on Good ground over 1m2½f. Saxony Charms is the only other horse with a genuine prominent profile and will likely track Garden Party in second or third, giving the race a relatively settled early shape rather than a contested gallop. With no other confirmed pace-maker to pressure Garden Party, she can dictate entirely on her own terms, conserving energy through the middle section before Moore decides when to ask. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or at worst in a close-up midfield position and produce a finish — true deep hold-up closers are at a structural disadvantage with a solo front-runner likely to control the fractions. The field contains more genuine hold-up types (Chosen One, Elusive In Mayo, Serendipia) than the map can comfortably accommodate at the rear; of those, Elusive In Mayo's high OR and Serendipia's form consistency make them the most likely to actually secure a competitive position, but all three will likely be racing out of their preferred role regardless.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Garden Party Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Party is allowed to bowl along uncontested and Ryan Moore produces a well-judged front-running display from the outset.
scenarios.body: Garden Party dictates a modest pace that makes the race entirely on her terms, with Saxony Charms the only horse close enough to apply any pressure — and even that may not materialise until late. Horses who travel prominently or in a close midfield berth without losing ground on the tempo will be best placed to challenge, but Garden Party's ability to kick again when she chooses makes her very hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Party's long layoff (291 days) catches up with her in the final two furlongs and she stops to nothing.
scenarios.body: Saxony Charms or Zadawa, travelling in touch throughout, would be ideally positioned to sweep past a tiring leader as the pace collapses in the closing stages. Horses who have settled close to the pace on a genuine run surface will pick up the pieces if Garden Party flatters to deceive on her comeback from a near ten-month absence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough midway through to string the field out and allow a well-ridden midfield runner to pick through.
scenarios.body: A pace collapse after a deceptively sharp early tempo would open a gap for a well-positioned midfield traveller like Serendipia or Chosen One to come through beaten horses inside the final furlong. However, this scenario is structurally discounted because the horses most likely to deliver it are redistributed hold-up types racing out of their natural position and not guaranteed the tactical setup they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong, the field is strung out, and true hold-up types can make up ground from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Elusive In Mayo or Trumph would need a fast enough gallop to create the gaps required to close from well back, which is unlikely given Garden Party's ability to control the fractions without being pressured. This scenario is heavily discounted because the principal beneficiaries are genuine hold-up horses who are likely to be crowded out of their preferred position by the number of similar types in the field.

watchPoints.text: Garden Party's 291-day layoff is the single biggest risk factor in the race — watch whether Ryan Moore chooses to conserve her early or whether any signs of rustiness emerge turning for home, as the entire pace scenario collapses if she stops.

The volume of hold-up horses (Chosen One, Elusive In Mayo, Serendipia, Salamina, Trumph, Quinchy Lady, Zadawa) relative to the limited pace in the race creates a serious crowding risk at the rear in the early stages — watch for traffic problems and horses unable to find clear daylight when the race begins to develop.

Saxony Charms with Colin Keane is the only genuine prominent-style horse positioned to benefit if Garden Party fails — watch whether Keane actively tracks the leader from flagfall or allows a gap to open, as the positioning in the first two furlongs will be critical.

Fairylike and The Blonde Lady are both unexposed debutantes for powerful yards (A P O'Brien and A J Martin respectively) — either could show a natural prominent or even front-running style that has not been flagged, which would add unscripted pressure to Garden Party's controlled gallop.

Elusive In Mayo's notably high OR of 120 relative to rivals rated 74-75 (Chosen One, Serendipia) suggests a rating disparity that may not reflect true ability given limited form — watch whether Nicola Burns (5) can find a tactical position that mitigates the redistribution issue.

races.name: Fitzgerald Construction Building 'A' Rated Homes Handicap

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for Cian Hughes on this 4yo who has won twice at 8f on Good and arrives only 8d since last run; confirmed front-runner with a high STYLE_FIT score meaning it is genuinely in its natural role here, and an uncontested lead on Good ground makes it dangerous despite a recent below-par run.

runners_data.name: Sheamus Seimhiu
runners_data.note: 291 days off the track is a significant concern for this hold-up performer who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish; its best form is on softer ground and its Good-ground record (0W0P from three) offers little encouragement on return.

runners_data.name: Half Cut
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for Anthony Mullins equipped with a tongue-strap, but its recent form over 10-12f suggests the step back to a mile may be sharp enough; Good-ground record reads 0W0P from three starts and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the worry.

runners_data.name: James Henry
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true rear position is occupied by so many others that he has been pushed into a mapped midfield slot he won't naturally fill; Chris Hayes knows the horse well, has placed form at 7-8f on Good, and if he can find a clear run two out, his finish is live.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this 3yo for Mrs Harrington, who has a sizeable book of form at the trip on Good ground including a win over 10f; hold-up style suits a big field if she can get a clear run, though her Good-ground conversion rate is modest at 1W3P from 11 attempts.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue-tie and ridden by a 3lb claimer, this 3yo won at 7f on Good and has shown consistent form at that distance; hold-up style in a field with no true pace means she could find herself further back than ideal, but the ability is there if a gap appears late.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is notable for Paul Flynn's yard; this 3yo wears a tongue-strap and hood combination, has placed form at 7f on Good, and its style as a hold-up horse places it at the mercy of traffic, though McMonagle's ability to find a run is an obvious asset.

runners_data.name: Mountain Memory
runners_data.note: Trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery, a notable combination, but this 3yo's form is limited — only one run on comparable Going (1/4 sim-going) — and the fade-in-finish flag alongside an OR of 59 suggests it will need things to fall perfectly from its hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Thompson Gunner
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse in true nature, bumped into a midfield map slot because the rear is overcrowded; ran just 2 days ago, which is a significant stamina query, and his form is primarily over 10f with a win on Standard surfaces rather than turf, making this a difficult assignment.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: This 8yo for W McCreery arrives 20 days fresh, but has a persistent fade-in-finish tendency and a win-less Good-ground record; being a true hold-up type forced into midfield on the map doesn't change that he will likely end up further back than ideal in a 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Ridden by a 7lb claimer Terry Casey for Mulvany, this 3yo has a tongue-tie and has shown placed form at 8-10f on Good; rated the second most prominent-style runner in the field, it may be best placed to press Launch Time and could benefit greatly if the pace collapses late.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to surplus closers in the field; OR of 44 and a record of 0W0P on Good over similar trips, combined with a fade-in-finish note, make it very hard to recommend as a winner regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Winston's Promise
runners_data.note: Liam Cusack's 3yo is fitted with a hood and has only three career starts, all resulting in 8th or worse; a genuine hold-up type whose redistribution into the midfield map slot understates how far back it will likely race, and the fade-in-finish flag is a further negative.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: An 8yo handicapper for Seamus Fahey, fitted with a hood and mapped out of its natural hold-up role; best form on Standard surfaces and Good-ground record reads 0W1P from eight attempts, making a winning performance in a 19-runner field at this level a very tall order.

runners_data.name: Lorr's Girl
runners_data.note: A tongue-and-blinkers combination on this 5yo for Rodger Sweeney (no runners in 14 days); a genuine late-runner pushed into a midfield position by field congestion, with one placed run from 15 Good-ground attempts suggesting the surface isn't the issue but talent and opportunity are.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's 8yo is fitted with a tongue-strap and blinkers and has placed three times at 8f on Good — arguably the best Good-ground conversion among the redistributed hold-up types; if the pace falls apart and a gap appears inside the final furlong, its tenacity could produce a minor place.

runners_data.name: Leannespour
runners_data.note: Edward Lynam's 3yo has shown one placed run from four starts, all at 6-7f, making this step to a mile a genuine question; fade-in-finish tendency and redistribution out of its natural hold-up slot mean it would need an unusually perfect trip to threaten.

runners_data.name: Starflow
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead sends out this 3yo wearing a tongue-tie and blinkers after a 74-day absence, which is the longest layoff in the field; Good-ground form is limited (2/4 sim-going) and the fade-in-finish flag combined with the return from a break makes this hard to support.

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 4yo ran just 2 days ago — the joint-shortest turnaround in the field alongside Thompson Gunner — and has placed form at 10f on Good including a win; a true hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map, and the quick return means fitness is not the query but pace shape and traffic are.

races.paceDynamic: Launch Time is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and, with no genuine rival to contest the lead, will control fractions from the off at a sustainable clip on Good ground over one mile at Cork. Borora Aura is the only other prominent-type likely to press forward, meaning Launch Time faces no meaningful pressure and can dictate every yard at a rhythm that suits its stamina profile. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up horses — James Henry, Thompson Gunner, Morning Approach, Winston's Promise, Peig Sayers, Jazz Dreamers, Mullacash Buzz, Lorr's Girl, Leannespour, Starflow and Reponse Finale are all true hold-up types who cannot all settle at the rear and will be shuffled into midfield against their nature; of these, James Henry and Thompson Gunner are most likely to negotiate a midfield berth closest to the action given their records at the trip. With a lone pace-setter operating unchallenged and the bulk of the field forced wide or into unfamiliar positions, this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit prominently or in a close-tracking midfield position and pounce in the straight, rather than deep closers who will face a wall of traffic off a steady gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Launch Time Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Launch Time bowls along uncontested at a controlled pace and the field is unable to reel it in from midfield.
scenarios.body: Launch Time, handled by Colin Keane for the in-form Cian Hughes yard, sets an untroubled rhythm and quickens enough turning for home to hold off pursuers on Good ground that suits; horses prominent or in a close-tracking position are best placed to chase it home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Trackers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly honest enough that one or two close-tracking midfield horses produce a sustained run through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Horses like Dawn Flame, Glamazon or Imnotleavinyou, who can sit within two or three lengths of the pace in a big field, get the clearest run and overhaul the leader in the closing stages; the key is a good position at the two-furlong pole without being shuffled wide.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Suits Few
scenarios.trigger: If the large field produces a stop-start pace with scrimmaging in the straight that leaves closers with nowhere to go.
scenarios.body: Redistributed hold-up horses that find clear daylight late — most plausibly James Henry or Mullacash Buzz, who have placed figures at this course and trip — emerge from the carnage to snatch a place at least; the scenario is structurally unlikely given how few are genuine late runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Swamped
scenarios.trigger: If Borora Aura or another prominent mover applies unexpected pressure early, turning the race into a truly run test.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run mile on Good ground would theoretically draw out closers, but because the bulk of the hold-up horses are redistributed out-of-role types lacking the natural position to sustain late runs, few benefit; Glamazon or Dawn Flame, with the stamina and good-ground records to handle a stronger gallop, are the most likely to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Launch Time (Keane/Hughes) has a completely uncontested lead in a 19-runner field — watch whether it is sent on at the start, because if it controls fractions at a canter, it will be very difficult to catch.

With 19 runners and a disproportionate number of hold-up types forced into midfield, watch for serious traffic problems in the final two furlongs; horses on the wide outside draw could be seriously inconvenienced.
Thompson Gunner and Reponse Finale both ran within the last 2 days — monitor market moves and early behaviour in the parade ring as quick turnarounds at this level can produce flat performances.

Borora Aura (Casey 7lb claim) is the only horse likely to apply any pressure to Launch Time early — if it tracks the leader within two lengths, watch whether it weakens or sustains its effort into the straight, as that dictates whether this becomes a true test or a solo procession.

The Cian Hughes yard has two runners (Launch Time and Thompson Gunner) — note which attracts the stronger support in the market, as stable confidence could be a useful guide in a wide-open 19-runner handicap.
